title: Nevada's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Nevada's 2nd Congressional District pits Republican David Flippo against Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson in the race to succeed retiring Republican Rep. Mark Amodei, who held the seat for 15 years. The district covers much of northern Nevada including Reno, and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+7; President Trump carried it by 14 points in 2024. Flippo, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel endorsed by President Trump, won a crowded Republican primary after a contentious contest against state-backed candidates. Benitez-Thompson, a former Nevada Assembly majority leader and social worker, won the Democratic primary and hopes to become the first Democrat ever to represent the district.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the general election matchup in Nevada's 2nd Congressional District as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the seat as Solid Republican (R+7).

candidates.name: David Flippo
candidates.summary: David Flippo is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and small business owner who won the Republican primary with President Trump's endorsement. He served 24 years in the Air Force commanding over 1,000 airmen and establishing bases in Iraq, later worked for BP in Alaska, and now owns a HobbyTown franchise and a financial advisory firm in Nevada. Flippo campaigns on conservative positions including immigration enforcement, energy independence, opposition to Shariah law, and support for Trump's agenda.

candidates.name: Teresa Benitez-Thompson
candidates.summary: Teresa Benitez-Thompson is a former Nevada Assembly majority leader and licensed social worker who won the Democratic primary to run for Congress. She served 12 years in the Nevada Assembly (2011-2021) representing Reno, rising to majority floor leader, and later served as chief of staff to Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford. Benitez-Thompson campaigns on expanding healthcare access, raising the minimum wage, lowering prescription drug costs, and bringing federal investment to northern Nevada.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on structural and historical factors. Nevada's 2nd District has a Cook PVI of R+7, and Donald Trump carried it by 14 points in 2024 — a strong recent Republican baseline. The district has never elected a Democrat to Congress. However, this is an open-seat contest due to Rep. Mark Amodei's retirement, and Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson is a credible recruit with state legislative leadership experience. Republican David Flippo won a crowded primary with Trump's endorsement and ran on a conservative platform. Without polling to test the race's competitiveness, the district's underlying partisanship makes Flippo the clear favorite, but Benitez-Thompson's profile and the open-seat nature prevent this from being rated safe. Confidence is medium due to the absence of any public polling data.
